newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil falls sharply.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil falls sharply.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil fell sharply on Friday, following in the footsteps of low sulphur which fell earlier in the week, traders said.

An Irish utility bought a cargo from an ARA player at $112 cif NWE, and a trader bought a Scandinavian-origin cargo from another trader at around $11.50. These numbers compare with offers at $116 cif NWE on Thursday.

High sulphur barges were also sharply weaker for most of the day, amid news that there was another problem at Esso's flexi-coker. Barges traded as low as $108 fob ARA in the early afternoon, then rose towards the day's end after the company said the problem had been a temporary one.
Low sulphur fuel oil was quieter, and steadier, following deals on Thursday at around $115.50 fob NWE, $116.
Swaps were steady to firmer by the day's end, heard bid at around $117 fob NWE for January.
